name: Black Springs
reason: A campground named in Coffin Bay NP's page (rule 2/3: a camp site, part of the park); the candidate's coordinates are in the Mid North, not Eyre.
objection: Parks SA names it, but only as a camp site.

name: Coffin Bay Oyster Walk
reason: Rule 1-2: regional tourism board names an 8 km signposted shoreline walk between Long Beach and Snapper Point with a Kellidie Bay lookout loop; walkable in sections.
objection: One counted source; a town foreshore path may be too minor.

name: Coffin Bay Oyster Farm Tours
reason: Operator tours, not a place (spot is a place, not a business); the Coffin Bay town/oyster walk covers the place.
objection: Oysters are Coffin Bay's signature draw and two sources list tours.

name: Yanerbie Sandhills
reason: Rule 1-3: two counted sources (tourism board, SATC) name giant white dunes along Westall Way to climb and sandboard; free, open access.
objection: Remote 20 min off the highway on gravel loop.

name: Elliston Coastal Trail
reason: Rule 1-2: tourism board describes a 13.6 km clifftop trail with the Cliffs of Elliston sculptures, shorter loop options.
objection: Single counted source; sculptures are partly modern public art.

name: Talia Caves
reason: Rule 1-2: tourism board names The Woolshed cavern (walkway and steps) and The Tub sea crater as stops on the coast; free.
objection: One counted source; short stop, rarely visited.

name: Mount Dutton Bay Woolshed Museum
reason: Heritage-listed 1875 woolshed with museum, tours by booking only ($10); a private property business. For: genuine heritage museum, tours. Against: bookings required, one source, seasonal.
objection: Not open on arrival; effectively an accommodation-and-tour property.

name: Anxious Bay
reason: No counted source names the bay as somewhere to go (no visitor listing found); a bay label, not a place to do something.
objection: 819 page views and it borders Elliston/Venus Bay coast.

name: Venus Bay Conservation Park
reason: Two counted sources (Parks SA, tourism board): Weyland Peninsula beaches, tombolo, 100+ bird species, fishing. For: park agency page, accessible beaches. Against: park pages offer no specific named sight; friend test only if nearby; partial closures.
objection: A generic conservation park; nothing named to see in half an hour.

name: Baird Bay Ocean Eco Experience
reason: Operator (swim with sea lions tour); the place is Baird Bay itself, which should be judged as a place, not this business.
objection: Wikivoyage names swimming with sea lions at Baird Bay as a headline draw.

name: Point Labatt Conservation Park
reason: Rule 1-3: Parks SA and tourism board name the only permanent mainland Australian sea lion colony, with a clifftop viewing platform; half-day trip.
objection: Remote, 50 km from Streaky Bay on partly unsealed road.

name: Sceale Bay
reason: Village and bay south of Streaky Bay; Point Labatt page gives access via Sceale Bay, tourism board points to Surfers Beach there. For: small coastal stop with beach. Against: counted source mentions it only as access point.
objection: The village is a gateway to Point Labatt, not a draw.

name: Laura Bay Conservation Park
reason: Tourism board lists sheltered bay with mangroves, bird feeding grounds, lookout and 1911 landing site. Against: one source, short visit, little to do.
objection: Obscure local reserve, seen only by bird watchers.

name: Streaky Bay Jetty
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage and tourism board name the renovated 350 m jetty, with swimming pool enclosure, for views and sunset.
objection: A jetty is common to every SA town.

name: Streaky Bay Museum
reason: Wikivoyage lists National Trust museum with historic vehicles. For: counted source, indoor stop. Against: one source, small-town museum, short visit; hours unclear.
objection: Only a local historical collection.

name: Streaky Bay Powerhouse Museum
reason: Tourism board: 400+ restored working engines, open Tue and Fri afternoons only. For: described as a must-visit engine display. Against: one source, two afternoons a week.
objection: Limited opening makes it unreliable when a visitor arrives.

name: Streaky Bay Great White Shark Replica
reason: Tourism board: 5 m fibreglass model, among the town's most photographed attractions (quirky roadside icon). Against: located inside a Shell service station, 10-minute stop, one source.
objection: It is a fixture of a petrol station, effectively a shop.

name: Streaky Bay Back Beach
reason: Surf beach 8 km from town per tourism board, but one source and it is a local surf break; Granites and Smooth Pool already cover the beach/rock-pool stops.
objection: Rock pools at low tide and sealed access make it a plausible second-tier beach.

name: Hally's Beach
reason: Duplicate: a stop on Cape Bauer Loop, which is judged as Cape Bauer; one source, short pull-out.
objection: Surf fishing lookout with boardwalk stairs, a named stop.

name: Surfers Beach Streaky Bay
reason: One source and a gentle local beach near Sceale Bay; no distinct draw beyond ordinary beach swimming.
objection: Sealed access, lookout, dolphins; tourism board gives it a page.

name: The Granites Streaky Bay
reason: Rule 1-3: tourism board names striking granite formations, sandy lagoon and rock pools with staircase access; 15 min from town.
objection: Single source.

name: Smooth Pool
reason: Tourism board: calm granite-shelf rock pools for swimming and snorkelling on Westall Way. For: a distinct natural pool. Against: one source, tide-dependent, unsealed access.
objection: Another similar beach stop near the Granites.

name: High Cliff
reason: Tourism board: clifftop lookout over the Southern Ocean on Westall Way, gravel access. Against: roadside lookout, one source, no path to the beach; may belong to the Westall Way loop.
objection: A pull-out unless a guide singles it out.

name: Whistling Rocks and the Blowholes
reason: Rule 1-3: tourism board calls it a must-see on Cape Bauer Loop, with a 360 m boardwalk to cliff platforms; best at high tide.
objection: Depends on swell and tide.

name: Kerrin McEvoy Bronze Statue
reason: Minor memorial/statue on the foreshore (rule 3); a ten-minute photo stop.
objection: A town-celebrated landmark with a page.

name: Streaky Bay Pioneers Park
reason: A town park with no named visitor draw (rule 2/3), one source.
objection: Foreshore park is where visitors picnic.

name: Smoky Bay Jetty
reason: A small-town jetty, one source and no named things to see or do (rule 2/3); Smoky Bay's oyster draw is separate.
objection: Jetty walks are a usual coast activity.

name: Smoky Bay Oyster Farm Tours
reason: Operator tour at an aquaculture park, not a place (spot is a place, not a business).
objection: Wikivoyage mentions the shed tour as an activity.

name: Nuyts Archipelago Conservation Park
reason: Tourism board: island group accessible only by boat, tour boats run to the islands. Against: needs a vessel, one source, vehicle/tour is not a spot; Franklin Islands prohibited. For: islands are a real destination.
objection: No self-reliant visitor access.

name: Acraman Creek Conservation Park
reason: Two counted sources: mangroves, canoeing, fishing, shorebirds west of Ceduna; for: named activities. Against: park agency generic text, boat launch use, little for a general visitor.
objection: Nothing singled out beyond a general reserve.

name: Cape Bauer
reason: Rule 1-3: tourism board's Cape Bauer Loop scenic drive covers the cape's panoramic views and Great Australian Bight cliffs; keep as the cape/loop (Hally's Beach and Whistling Rocks are separate stops).
objection: Overlaps Whistling Rocks as a stop on the same loop.

name: Ceduna Jetty
reason: Wikivoyage and tourism board: long pier with ocean and beach views. For: two counted sources. Against: a jetty; a short walk.
objection: Every SA town has a jetty.

name: Ceduna Museum
reason: Wikivoyage and tourism board list the National Trust museum ($3.50, 10am to noon). For: two sources. Against: very limited hours, small local museum.
objection: A short-hours local museum.

name: Ceduna Aboriginal Arts and Culture Centre
reason: Wikivoyage lists Tjutjuna Arts (Mon-Fri, art display and sale), though link is dead. For: Aboriginal art gallery. Against: one source, mostly a shop and the listing may be stale.
objection: May be a retail outlet only.

name: Oysterfest
reason: Annual festival, not a permanent place (rule 4).
objection: Ceduna's best-known event.

name: Denial Bay Jetty
reason: One source, local jetty; no named draw (rule 2/3).
objection: Historic jetty near the oyster beds.

name: Pinky Point Lookout
reason: Rule 1-2: tourism board names a lookout over the wharf, islands and channel at the end of the Encounter walking trail, with the Eleni K wreck anchor and sunset views; accessible.
objection: Single source, short stop.

name: Penong Windmill Museum
reason: Rule 1-3: tourism board and Wikivoyage name an outdoor museum of about 20 windmills, with Australia's largest windmill, beside the highway; free, quirky icon.
objection: About a half-hour stop.

name: OTC Satellite Earth Station
reason: Tourism board: 1969 satellite station, unmanned, visitors walk the perimeter fence 34 km from Ceduna. For: history. Against: perimeter-fence view only, one source.
objection: Exterior-only, no entry.

name: Fowlers Bay Conservation Park
reason: Rule 1-3: Parks SA and tourism board name giant sand dunes at Fowlers Bay, Scotts Beach, Mexican Hat; wildlife and whales.
objection: Remote, 4WD sections.

name: Scotts Beach
reason: Duplicate: a beach and campground inside Fowlers Bay Conservation Park (kept as one); coordinates in the candidate are in New Zealand and wrong.
objection: Named separately by Parks SA.

name: Mexican Hat
reason: Duplicate: headland and campground within Fowlers Bay Conservation Park.
objection: Parks SA names it.

name: Fowlers Bay Whale Watching
reason: Operator tours; the place is Fowlers Bay, which the park/dunes candidate covers.
objection: Southern right whales June to October are a headline draw on the southaustralia.com page.

name: Great Australian Bight Marine Park
reason: A marine park along the Nullarbor coast with no single visitor point; whale viewing is at Head of Bight, which is a place to judge separately.
objection: SATC names the park.

name: Yalata Roadhouse
reason: A roadhouse (business, rule 2).
objection: Eyre Highway rest stop with an animal crossing sign.

name: Nullarbor Plain
reason: Wikivoyage Eyre Peninsula names it; high interest (88k views). For: iconic outback region. Against: an area crossed by highway rather than a single place; visitors' real stops are Bunda Cliffs, Head of Bight and roadhouses.
objection: A region, not a place a visitor can do something at.

name: Koonalda Cave
reason: Aboriginal heritage cave with restricted access (rule 2); no counted visitor source found.
objection: Famous archaeological site.

name: Nullarbor Links
reason: An 18-hole course strung along 1,365 km of highway across two states, a route of roadhouse holes rather than one place; one source (SATC).
objection: Quirky icon; nearly 15k page views.

name: Googs Track
reason: Parks SA and tour page name a 4WD desert track north of Ceduna through Yellabinna, ending at Goog's Lake. For: two counted sources, a real outback drive. Against: 4WD-only, remote, mostly accessed through tours.
objection: Not accessible to normal visitors.

name: Yumbarra Conservation Park
reason: Remote park with no named facility, duplicate of the Googs Track area (it lies on the track); counted sources are generic.
objection: Two counted sources name it.
